2609.21247.title: When Does Reasoning Help in Machine Translation? A Hierarchical Analysis of LRM Reasoning Traces
2609.21247.paper_summary: Large Reasoning Models increasingly use intermediate traces for machine translation, but it remains unclear when such reasoning helps or hurts. We analyze reasoning traces across models, languages, domains, and datasets, focusing on reasoning language, length, and structure. We find that the best reasoning language is model-specific, reasoning length has a non-monotonic relationship with quality, and traces exhibit recurring functional patterns. To uncover these patterns, we introduce Hierarchical Meta-Summarization (HMS), a scalable framework that induces coarse- and fine-grained reasoning structures without predefined taxonomies. HMS reveals a shared organization--understanding/planning, translating/drafting, and refining/verifying--alongside domain-specific variation. Our results suggest that MT reasoning should be controlled in a model-aware, length-aware, and pattern-aware manner rather than uniformly encouraged.
2609.21247.paper_summary_zh: 大型推理模型越來越多地使用中間痕跡進行機器翻譯，但何時這種推理有助於或有害仍不明朗。<lb/>我們分析了不同模型、語言、領域和數據集中的推理痕跡，重點關注推理語言、長度和結構。<lb/>我們發現最佳的推理語言是特定於模型的，推理長度與質量之間存在非單調關係，且痕跡顯示出重複的功能模式。<lb/>為了揭示這些模式，我們引入了層次化元摘要（HMS），這是一個可擴展的框架，可以在沒有預定分類法的情況下誘導粗略和細緻的推理結構。<lb/>HMS揭示了一種共享的組織結構——理解/規劃、翻譯/草擬和精煉/驗證——以及特定於領域的變化。<lb/>我們的結果表明，機器翻譯推理應以模型感知、長度感知和模式感知的方式進行控制，而不是均勻鼓勵。
